reason: A 48-stop Tab walk on settings.referrals records each stop's document position: the status badges run top to bottom (Applied in the Razer Capital row, then Started in the next row, Pluto Import and Export), matching the DOM and the visual order. The backward jump the sweep read is a scroll artifact: reaching Started scrolls the _layout container by 385px, so its viewport y falls from 878 to 544. Separately, focus drops to the page body about 11ms after landing on Started, so one Tab press shows no focus; that is a focus-loss problem, not a reordering.

The flagged element is the Payout column header: a plain th child div with a pointer cursor and a click handler, no tabindex, no button inside and no aria-sort. Clicking it re-sorts the referral rows (a chevron moves to Payout), but the focus probe cannot reach it (visible: false, via: null) and focus() leaves focus on the body, so keyboard users cannot sort by any column. Every row stays readable, so the task is possible but harder: medium.
